_purpose: Frozen Wave-0 baseline for the 3D Breakthrough Program (docs/3d_breakthrough_master_plan.md). Every Wave 1+ agent's acceptance gates are measured against this file, not against docs/etkdg_3d_gap_rfc.md's original numbers directly (those numbers are reproduced byte-identically at current HEAD in the deterministic block below, confirming the RFC's diagnosis is still valid and unchanged as of v0.7.0).

meta.methodology_note: Ran scripts/etkdg_vs_rdkit_gap.py as 5 independent fresh Python process invocations (not 5 loop iterations in one process), matching this project's own issue #70 pseudo-replication lesson: process-level independence is required before treating repeated measurements as corroborating evidence, since a single process's internal state can mask environment-level noise. Raw per-run summaries are preserved at validation/results/etkdg_baseline_history/run{1..5}_summary.json and run{1..5}_rows.jsonl. The pre-existing committed baseline (validation/results/etkdg_vs_rdkit_summary.json / _rows.jsonl, as authored by the original RFC) was copied aside to etkdg_vs_rdkit_{summary,rows}.RFC-original.{json,jsonl} before this rerun overwrote them.

rfc_reproduction_check.detail: All 5 fresh-process reruns at current HEAD (v0.7.0) reproduced the RFC's original geometrically_valid_rate (25.9%, 15/58 ok, 39/58 bond-length-blowup, 4/58 gross-clash) and every other deterministic metric byte-identically. The RFC was originally measured against an older build (chematic 0.6.0 in the venv before this baseline rebuilt it to 0.7.0); this baseline confirms the diagnosed defect is unchanged by any commit between that measurement and 9f9f459 -- it is a live, unresolved gap, not a stale claim.

deterministic_metrics_frozen._note: Every field below was byte-identical across all 5 independent process runs (single-conformer path, noise_sigma_deg=0.0) -- safe to freeze as a single value and diff Wave 1+ results against directly.

raw_embed_returned_rate.note: fraction where the embedder returned finite, non-clashing coordinates at all -- does NOT check geometric validity (bond lengths etc). See geometrically_valid_rate for that.

geometrically_valid_rate.note: fraction of the whole corpus that produced a geometry passing the >50%-of-covalent-reference bond-length check (status == 'ok'). This is the metric that should be called 'success' -- raw_embed_returned_rate alone is misleadingly high because chematic's coordinate generator never refuses to return coordinates, it just sometimes returns a torn structure.

fair_mmff94_energy_delta_chematic_minus_.note: positive = chematic's own conformer scores WORSE than RDKit's geometry under chematic's own full MMFF94 breakdown (same topology, same energy function -- an apples-to-apples geometry-quality signal, not an absolute energy comparison).

chirality_all_geometry.note: Rolled up over EVERY declared stereocenter reached, including torn (chematic_bond_length_blowup) geometry. A signed-volume or dihedral-sign read on a torn molecule conflates 'no stereo enforcement' with 'garbage geometry' -- use chirality_clean_geometry for the unconfounded match-rate signal; this block is provided for coverage (which is a structural fact independent of geometry quality) and for transparency, not for the match-rate column.

chirality_clean_geometry.note: Same rollup restricted to status=='ok' rows only (no bond >50% off the covalent-radius reference). Small n by construction -- Phase 0's blow-up bug (see docs/etkdg_3d_gap_rfc.md) removed most of the tetrahedral-4-heavy and alkene rows from this subset -- but this is the only match-rate signal not confounded by torn geometry.

runtime_metrics_non_frozen._note: Wall-clock timing varies run-to-run (machine noise, same shape as issue #70) -- recorded as mean/stdev/min/max across the 5 runs, NOT a single frozen value. A Wave 1+ agent's runtime claim must be measured the same way (>=5 independent process runs) before comparing against this spread.

ensemble_metrics_observed_not_contracted._note: IMPORTANT for Agent C: chematic-3d's PRNG (prng.rs) self-seeds from a process-global atomic counter with NO public seed parameter today. The script's own meta.reproducibility_note (see raw run files) states ensemble diversity/duplicate-rate figures are 'not bit-reproducible run-to-run' -- but empirically, all 5 independent process runs in this baseline produced BIT-IDENTICAL chematic_n_kept and chematic_diversity values for every one of the 8 ENSEMBLE_SUBSET molecules. This is recorded as an OBSERVATION, not a guarantee: the atomic counter most likely starts from the same fixed compile-time value on every fresh process and the code path is single-threaded and call-order-deterministic today, so apparent stability is coincidental to the current single-threaded, single-process-per-run usage pattern, not a contracted property. EmbedParameters.random_seed (Wave 1, Agent C) must add an EXPLICIT, public, call-local seed -- do not treat this observed stability as removing that requirement.

known_dead_or_unwired_code_confirmed_pre.dg_fft.rs: Present, ~840 lines, #![allow(dead_code)], zero callers workspace-wide (confirmed: grep -rn 'generate_coords_dg\b' returns only its own definition/tests). This is Agent C's primary starting point per the RFC.
known_dead_or_unwired_code_confirmed_pre.stereo3d.rs: Present, 471 lines, NOT dead -- assign_stereo_from_3d is exported from lib.rs and used by this very gap script (cm.stereo_from_coords) to perceive stereo FROM a 3D geometry. This is the opposite direction from what Agent D needs (enforcing DECLARED stereo AS a constraint during embedding) -- Agent D should not assume this file already solves its problem.
known_dead_or_unwired_code_confirmed_pre.chematic-ff full MMFF94/UFF: Present and complete (bond/angle/oop_stbn/torsion/vdw + L-BFGS), confirmed NOT called by chematic-3d/src/minimize.rs, which hand-rolls a smaller bond+angle+VdW-only energy function. Agent F's primary target.
